speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how the vertigo feels—does it seem like the room is spinning around you, or do you feel like you are swaying? Also, did this episode start suddenly while you were resting or during a specific head movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear? Also, does moving your head in a specific direction, such as looking up or rolling over in bed, trigger the spinning sensation again?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the episode lasted about three minutes, which is quite short. Did you notice if turning your head to the left or right, or rolling over in bed, reliably triggered the spinning again? Also, have you had any recent head trauma or upper respiratory infections?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.
